citations.long: There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.

citations.short: Contamination, chemical or physical change, deterioration
citations.long: An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning significant chemical, physical, or other change or deterioration in a distributed drug product.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Written procedures are not established and followed for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment, including utensils, used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.

citations.short: Instruments, apparatus, et. al. not meeting specs
citations.long: The use of instruments not meeting established specifications was observed.
The statistical quality control criteria fail to include appropriate acceptance levels.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
The suitability of all testing methods is not verified under actual conditions of use.
Employees are not given training in the particular operations they perform as part of their function.

citations.short: Description of containers, labels, et. al.
citations.long: Master production and control records lack a description of the drug product containers, closures and packaging materials, a specimen or copy of each label and all other labeling, and the signatures and dates entered by the person or persons responsible for the approval of labeling.
Written procedures have not been developed for the receipt and reporting to FDA of post marketing adverse drug experiences.

citations.short: Failure by applicant to report ADE
citations.long: Adverse drug experience information has not been reported to FDA.

Periodic reports of non-alert adverse drug experiences have not been submitted quarterly for an application which was approved less than three years ago and yearly for an application which was approved three or more years ago.
An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning an incident that caused a drug product or its labeling to be applied to another article.
An annual report was not submitted within 60 days of the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application to the FDA division responsible for reviewing the application.
An annual report did not include a brief summary of significant new information from the previous year that might affect the safety, effectiveness, or labeling of the drug product.
